# 0131 — Pre-generate comprehension questions for parent-uploaded exercises, reviewed by the parent, generated by a process that never holds the LLM key in Parent Controls

Date: 2026-10-28

Status: Accepted

## Context

User request: when a parent uploads a reading exercise (homework),
generate its 1-2 comprehension questions with an LLM right away
instead of live during the child's own session -- so that by the
time the child actually reads it, the questions are already there
(reducing a live LLM call) -- and show them to the parent in Parent
Controls for approval first.

Follow-up concern, and the harder design constraint this decision is
actually about: Parent Controls (`parent_controls/app.py`) is a plain
Flask app, reachable from any device on the LAN (decision 0002), and
today has **zero LLM imports anywhere in it** -- confirmed directly
(`grep` of its own imports). It should stay that way: it's the one
surface here reachable from outside this device, so it's the one
surface that should never hold an LLM API key. Generation has to
happen in a separate process that already has the key (the same
`OpenAILanguageModelBackend` + `config/loader.py` env loading
`voice_loop_demo.py` uses), talking to the parent only through the
shared sqlite db -- never through Flask.

Confirmed directly in the real code before building anything: a
`GeneratedBook.comprehension: list[tuple[str, str | None]]` field
already exists and already lets `_run_comprehension_questions()`
(`voice_loop_demo.py`) skip its own live `generate_comprehension_questions()`
call entirely when questions are already known -- that's exactly how
`story_library.py`'s hand-authored books work today (decisions
0104/0126). This feature is a second producer of that same field, not
a new mechanism.

## What shipped

**Schema** (`reading_exercises.py` + `storage/migrations.py`):
`ReadingExerciseRecord` gains `comprehension_status` ("pending" ->
"generated" -> "approved", or "failed"), `comprehension_questions`
(list of strings, same `\x1f`-joined flat-column convention
`reading/repository.py`'s `sight_words` already uses),
`comprehension_generated_at`, `comprehension_approved_at`.
`ReadingExerciseRepository` gains `list_awaiting_generation()`
(global, across every child -- the worker is one process polling the
whole db), `save_generated_questions()`, `mark_generation_failed()`,
`approve_questions()` (a parent's own edited text, not necessarily
the worker's verbatim output), `request_regeneration()` (resets back
to "pending").

**The worker** (new `parent_controls/comprehension_worker.py`): a
headless script, its own process, polling every 20s by default. For
each "pending" exercise, looks up the child's own profile for `age`
(falls back to 6, same default `_run_reading_partner()` itself uses
with none), calls `ConversationService.generate_comprehension_questions()`
(same call, same `check_speech()` screening, `_run_comprehension_questions()`
already used live) and saves the result as "generated." Nothing
usable (every candidate dropped, or the call raised) is marked
"failed" rather than left "pending," so the exact same content isn't
retried every single 20s poll -- a parent's explicit "regenerate"
tries again. New `scripts/run_comprehension_worker.sh`, meant for
cron/systemd on the Pi, independent of whether `voice_loop_demo.py`
is even running: a parent can upload an exercise with the child's
device off and still see generated questions next time they open
Parent Controls.

**Parent review** (`parent_controls/app.py` + `reading_exercises.html`):
two new routes, `approve-questions` (parent-submitted textarea,
possibly edited, -> `approve_questions()`) and `regenerate-questions`
(-> `request_regeneration()`) -- neither one makes an LLM call; both
just read/write the same repository the worker and Flask app both
already share. The template shows each exercise's own status:
"generating..." (pending), an editable textarea + Approve/Regenerate
buttons (generated), the approved list read-only + a Regenerate
option (approved), or a retry button (failed).

**Runtime** (`voice_loop_demo.py`): new `_approved_comprehension_pairs(exercise)`
returns `[(q, None) for q in exercise.comprehension_questions]` only
when `comprehension_status == "approved"` -- "generated" and "failed"
return `[]`, same as no comprehension at all, so
`_run_comprehension_questions()` falls straight back to its existing
live-generation path if a parent hasn't reviewed yet, or the worker
hasn't run yet. Wired into both of `_run_reading_partner()`'s own
`GeneratedBook` constructions (a fresh exercise and a reread). No
evidence sentence is produced (unlike `story_library.py`'s
hand-authored pairs) -- same as any other LLM-generated question
today.

## Consequences

- Reading Partner's live comprehension-question LLM call is skipped
  for any exercise a parent has approved ahead of time, the latency
  win the request asked for.
- Parent Controls' own process never imports an LLM backend, before
  or after this change -- the new routes only touch the repository.
- A parent sees nothing to review until the worker's next poll runs
  (up to ~20s, not instant-on-upload) -- the deliberate tradeoff for
  keeping the key out of the LAN-facing process rather than having
  Flask spawn or call anything itself.
- `_run_reading_partner_v2` (decision 0075, default OFF) wasn't
  touched -- same "out of scope, never had comprehension questions
  ported to it at all" precedent decision 0128 already established.

## Not yet done

- No UI surfacing of "age used for generation came from the child's
  profile" or a way to regenerate for a *different* age -- not asked
  for.
- The worker's poll interval is a fixed constant, not parent-
  configurable.
- `request_regeneration()` discards whatever was previously
  generated/approved outright rather than keeping history -- not
  asked for, and this project doesn't version anything else either.
